Acknowledged reach-plan-revision-adopted-20261023. My actual next action: build the eight-start baseline as an extension of the existing replay tool, file-only. The r2 package is kept as a held candidate. Nothing runs from this message.

PROCESS IDENTITIES, reconciled at 6:04 PM: no trainer and no owner is running. The admission tests row preflight_adoption_successor_b3_focused_check ended PASS at 5:48 PM. The supervisor's control file reads pause.

R2 CANDIDATE
- Admission change b3: reviewed twice. Its registered tests passed: 598 passed, and each of the two deliberate code breaks made all its named tests fail.
- The second review's two required items are in the binding tools only:
  - the replacement's gate exceptions must cite each branch's new decision, not the first attempt's;
  - a decision must be a message from the overseer to the builder that names the branch.
  The design agent is making those two fixes now.
- I stopped further admission changes (a b4 variant), per your message.
- Runtime held pending the baseline decision.

THE TOOL TO EXTEND: physical_comparison.py on branch repair/whole-body-request-2026-10-21 (2,013 lines, sha256 a541224d...). It is not in main's checkout. It already does the hard parts:
- World restores a complete saved world from an episode companion.
- replay() feeds the recorded command, mask, hand joint goal and eye command through BridgeEnv.step, 5 physics steps per model step, as the trainer did, with no learner.
- The binding checks the replayed start against the record: the 15 scored parts' mean orientation angle, the contact pairs, and the contact places.
- run_arm holds one command from one snapshot. Every arm gets the identical restored physics, controller and smoothing state.
- feasible_command builds a direct command from a target pose: the target's handle rows placed on the start's root, with the original strengths and mask.
- A repeat arm must reproduce its position and velocity digest.
- It has a memory stop and the power-throttling opt-out, and runs through test_runner.run_command.

THE DELTA (smallest; the original file kept as it is; a copy in a new D1 attempt package with a diff):
1. Inputs become parameters (run, start checkpoint, episode companion, recording, body, start step) in place of the fixed body 5, step 483,120 and the seg41j paths.
2. Selection, written before any run: for each body 0 to 7, the earliest model step of the a2 run where its causal chain records a new planner command with a recorded target and a complete observer record. Every exclusion is written with its cause.
3. Two arms per body from one replayed snapshot:
   - P: the recorded planner command, held 60 model steps (3 s);
   - D: the direct command from the same target pose, held 60 model steps.
   Same target, motor strengths, mask, smoothing and duration.
4. Readings:
   - Each hand's distance from a fixed palm point (the hand body's origin, as judge.py's end palm distance uses) to the same point in the target pose, at model steps 5, 10, 20 and 40 (0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2 s), and at every step to 60.
   - Arrived: both hands within 2 cm. Stayed: within 2 cm at every model step for 20 model steps after arriving by 2 s. One-hand results beside these.
   - The existing whole-body error E, falls (trunk roll and root height) and contacts other than the floor.
   - The recorded forecast compared over the first 5 model steps only. The later movement is labelled as two held commands, not replanning.
5. Budget: one clock over everything. Before each next body: stop when the time left is below the last body's measured time plus a closure reserve. Partial results are kept, the row closes, and the result states how many bodies ran.

PRESERVED INPUTS, to be pinned by sha256 in the package before any run:
- The a2 run: D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_preserved/s4r_pose_learning_S4R_pose_learning_a2_496250/run (causal_chain.jsonl, observer/ with model and world; args.json resume ...ckpt_step_496250, max_steps 496350, n_envs 8).
- Its complete start state: D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_preserved/s4r_measure_S4R_measure_496000/run/checkpoints/ckpt_step_496250 and episode_companion/ckpt_step_496250_f3b30525....pt.gz.
- Unknown, read during the build:
  - whether the a2 observer recordings hold full positions and contacts per model step for all eight bodies (the binding needs them; observer/world's chunk headers will show it);
  - which target each planning start's command aimed at (the causal chain's goal record per body).
  If either is missing, that is the concrete blocker, and the fallback is the plan's: capture exact starts in the next authorized learning run.

REPLAY MISMATCH PROPOSAL, for you to set before any result:
1. The existing binding, per body at its start step:
   - mean angle over the 15 scored parts at or below one tenth of the parts' turn in that command's own 250 ms;
   - the contact pairs exactly the recorded pairs;
   - each contact place within the existing CONTACT_PLACE_CM line.
2. New: each hand's palm point within 0.2 cm of the recorded one (one tenth of the 2 cm arrival line).
3. A body failing 1 or 2 is reported with its readings labelled "replayed start differs" and gives no winner.
4. A winner for a body only when its two arms' final palm distances differ by more than twice that body's palm mismatch, with the repeat arm's digest equal.

BOUNDED COST
- One 900 s executable budget, including loading, the fidelity checks, retries and closure.
- Measured comparable: row whole_body_request_comparison_483120 (Oct 21) took 202.2 s for one body: loading, a 1,320-model-step replay and its arms.
- The a2 starts lie within its 100 model steps (496,250 to 496,350), so each replay is shorter. The run stops by the rule above rather than splitting rows.
- Preparation and review time: no estimate.

Next, file-only:
- a D1 attempt via lifecycle prepare;
- the copy and the delta;
- the package pins;
- the registry row, before any run;
- independent review of the delta and package.
Then the package goes to you for a runtime decision. I will record this plan, its dependencies and "r2 runtime held pending the baseline decision" in the D1 work record. Execution owner: the builder; decision owner: the overseer.

Question: which file is "the existing capability/planner action record" whose next-action pointer you want updated? I read it as the D1 work record's next_action, which holds uncommitted keys of yours. I will not overwrite those without your word.
